title: A long-time member with no routines is greeted as a beginner with 'Make your first routine'
what: The 'Make your first routine' card shows to anyone with no routines who never saw it before, judged only by routines. A member who has logged months of workouts without routines, or who used routines and deleted them all before this version came out, gets the beginner card after updating: 'A routine is the list of exercises you do on one day. We will help you make one in 4 short steps.'
expected: Members who already train in the app are not taught what a routine is; the card shows only to members with little or no history, or uses words that fit someone who already logs workouts.
how_often: once per member, after the update
fix_line: Also look at how many workouts the member has logged before showing the beginner card.

items.reason: Fresh install: settings start on defaults; an update keeps saved settings through a numbered migration (Previous values and In use switch reset once, on purpose, owner R-61 and R-304) and unknown stored choices fall back safely. A newer exercise demo clip has its version in the file name, so it replaces the old download. Older workout drafts read as weight x reps. Old imported workout times are moved once, and again after restoring an older backup; logged and past workouts avoid that repair by never starting on a whole second. A gym server without the workout-of-the-day feature just hides the card. Sideload vs Play, watch-vs-phone versions and panel cache: nothing in these parts (the watch start card is in the other half of this folder). Whether workouts saved by much older versions all avoid the clock repair needs the version history (no git in this audit).

Plan end or leaving the gym: the gym's workout-of-the-day card checks the gym link and the gym's plan feature every read and disappears; the day key is the phone's own date, so a new day reads again. App not opened for 6 months (or Plus ended): the exercise chart opens on a year or all time without the free-plan check (existing findings). Year end and leap day: calendars and month grids use real date maths, so 29 Feb and January's previous-year step work; old records show their year. The workout-of-the-day still saying Start after it was done is an existing finding. Trial end, staff leaving and owner changing phone: nothing in these parts.

New-only flows here: the first-routine guide (marked done for anyone seen with routines), the settings migration (runs for every existing install), and the imported-times repair (runs once for every existing install). None is new-installs-only.
Existing users are covered by the migration and the one-time repair at start-up; the guide is shown to existing members without routines too.
No existing-user gap found in these parts.

No 'new since your last version' dots or notices live in these parts. A brand-new member's first workout sets bests without record pop-ups; the demo hides the first-routine card; a brand-new member sees the first-routine card, which fits them.
The beginner 'Make your first routine' card shows to long-time members with no routines after the update.
